children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares ended lower after hitting a three-week high on Tuesday, as retail investors booked profits.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed down 40.87 points, or 0.58%, at 6,954.52, after three consecutive sessions of gains.
** Earlier in the session, it rose as much as 2.5% to the highest level since August 18.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
slipped 0.19%, reversing an earlier gain of more than 3%, while peer SK Hynix
closed up 0.56%, after rising as much as 6% earlier.
** "The KOSPI turned lower on profit-taking by retail investors amid no major market-moving factor," said Seo Sang-young, an analyst at Mirae Asset Securities.
** South Korea's economy grew 0.6% in the second quarter from the preceding three months, revised central bank data showed, unchanged from the advance estimate in late July.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 3.86%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 2.04% and down 2.34%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 2.09%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 1.77%.
** Of the total 910 traded issues, 231 shares advanced, while 634 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 631.6 billion won ($469.71 million), while retail investors sold 3 trillion won.
** The won was quoted at 1,345.6 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.08% higher than its previous close at 1,346.7.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) were unchanged at 103.12.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 0.3 basis points to 3.901%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
rose by 2.0 basis points to 4.401%.
